---
title: "Privacy"
description: "What personal data PopuliVerse handles, and what it does not."
---

Last updated: 16 November 2026

PopuliVerse collects as little personal data as it can. Reading the site needs no account. There is no comments section and no advertising.

## Who Is Responsible

Khayyam RZAZADE, editor of PopuliVerse. Contact: editor@populiverse.com

## When You Visit

**Hosting.** The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. To deliver the pages, GitHub processes technical data such as your IP address.

**Visit statistics.** The site counts visits in two ways. Cloudflare Web Analytics loads one small script on each page. It sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser. A small counter run by the editor on Cloudflare adds one to a running total when you arrive, and your browser tab keeps your visit number until you close the tab, so you are counted once for each visit. The counter keeps the total and nothing about you.

**Everything else.** All other things the pages need, the typeface included, are served from this site itself. Reading the site sets no cookies.

## The Workspace

The Workspace is a place of your own on the site. Using it is up to you. You can try it as a guest or keep your work in an account.

**What an account holds.** Your email, your name and your institution. Your position and your field, which can be Prefer Not to Respond, and the words you type if you choose Other. Your research interests in one line, if you write them. Your answer to the question on writing for the Commentary, and the day you answered it. Your ORCID iD, if you connect it. The pages you write and the drafts you write. Your projects, each with its title, its question and what you put in it. What you save on the site, which can be a work, a Monitor item, an actor, a country or a chart, and with each of them the note you write on it, the tags you give it, whether you have read it and the passages you mark in it. For a work you save, the abstract as the Library had it that day, so that the passages you mark have a text to sit in. For each thing you save, the reference the site itself gives for it, which is what a draft's reference list is built from. A chart you send to Write is kept as the picture the page drew that day, with that page's own source line. The day you signed up and the day you last used it.

**A guest.** A guest gives no name and no email. The work is stored like an account's and can be opened from that browser only. It is lost when you sign out, clear the browser or change device, and is deleted 30 days after your last visit. A guest keeps at most 50 saved things, 20 pages, 3 projects, 3 drafts and 3 charts sent to Write.

**Where it is kept.** In a database the editor runs on his own account at Cloudflare, a company based in the United States. The sign-in codes are sent by Cloudflare's email service. Cloudflare keeps backups of the database for 30 days and short technical records of requests for a few days.

**What the editor counts.** The editor counts accounts and how they are used: how many people sign up, from which institutions and countries, in which positions and fields.

**Writing for the Commentary.** When you sign up you answer one question, whether you would like to write for the Commentary. If you answer Yes or Maybe Later, the editor sees your name, your email, your institution, your position, your field and your research interests together with your answer, and may write to you about writing a piece. If you answer No, the answer is counted and nothing else happens. You can change the answer on your account page whenever you like.

**Signing in.** There are no passwords. You sign in with a code sent to your email, or with ORCID once you have connected it. ORCID tells the Workspace your ORCID iD and your name, and nothing else.

**Against misuse.** With each sign-in, a guest's too, the Workspace keeps the IP address and the type of browser until a week after the sign-in ends. It counts the codes asked for an address for one day.

**Your institution.** When you look up your institution, the letters you type go to ROR, the open registry of research institutions, through the Workspace. Nothing else about you goes with them.

**One cookie.** When you sign in, or start as a guest, the Workspace sets one cookie that keeps you signed in. It holds a random key and nothing about you. It lasts 30 days after your last visit. The Workspace cannot work without it, so there is no cookie banner. While you sign in with ORCID, a second cookie lives for five minutes.

**Marks in your browser.** Signing in also leaves one plain mark in that browser, so that the pages of the site know to show Save and Note. It says that someone is signed in here, and nothing else. Signing out takes it away. While it is not there, no page of the site asks the Workspace anything. Opening the Workspace leaves a second plain mark saying that the Workspace is open to everyone, which is how the other pages of the site know they can offer Save and Note before you sign in. If you hide the note at the top of the Workspace, that browser keeps a third mark so the note stays hidden. Neither of them says anything about you.

**The newsletter box.** If you tick it when you sign up, your email and name go to Sender for the newsletter (see below). The box is never ticked for you.

**Download and delete.** On your account page, Download Everything gives you one file with your account, your shelf, your notes, all your pages, your drafts, your projects and the charts you sent to Write. Delete My Account deletes the account and everything in it at once. The backups at Cloudflare are gone 30 days later. Deleting the account does not end the newsletter: use the link in any newsletter for that.

**Accounts no longer used.** An account is kept as long as it is used. After two years without a sign-in, the Workspace sends one email. If the account is still not used 30 days later, it is deleted with everything in it.

## When You Write, Subscribe or Submit

**Email.** Messages to editor@populiverse.com are forwarded through Cloudflare to the editor's inbox. A message is kept for as long as it takes to deal with it.

**Newsletter.** The newsletter is sent with Sender, an email service based in Lithuania, in the EU. If you sign up, Sender keeps your email address for the editor, and it is used only to send you the monthly newsletter. Sender notes whether its emails are opened and which links are clicked, and your confirmation is recorded that way. Every newsletter has a link to unsubscribe, or you can write to the editor.

**Commentary authors.** Pieces are submitted through a form run by Tally, a form service based in Belgium, in the EU. Tally keeps what you send, your details and your file, for the editor. An author's name and affiliation, and the ORCID iD if one is given, are published with the piece and deposited with it in Zenodo.

## Your Rights

You can ask to see, correct or delete the personal data held about you. Write to the address above. In the Workspace you can also download or delete it yourself, on your account page.

## Changes to This Page

This page is updated whenever the site changes how it handles personal data.
